type_of: ResearchLoop run ownership and checkpoint lifecycle
name: ResearchLoop::new and ResearchLoop::resume

test_list.description: A second ResearchLoop using an independently opened CheckpointStore for the same program and root cannot own the active run.
ResearchLoop::new does not overwrite a checkpoint after the original loop has been dropped; callers must use resume.
Dropping the loop releases its lifetime owner lease and an explicit resume can continue the existing checkpoint.
A separate child process that owns the run is killed; the parent can then resume without consulting stale PID metadata.

inputs.name: store
inputs.description: A separately opened store handle for the program's persistent state root.

output_description: A single active loop owner for a root, with new-run creation refused when a checkpoint already exists and resume explicitly supported after lease release.
